_note: THE LIKENESS CORE, now subject-agnostic (v2). v1 hard-coded Carey's LoRA into the recipe; v2 moves identity to the SUBJECT PROFILE (handoff §3: the profile is the identity truth, engines consume it through adapters). The worker resolves profiles/<subject>/profile.json -> identity_packs.sdxl for the LoRA and references.ground_truth for the FaceID photo, so the SAME recipe generates Carey or anyone added through People. subject_profile here is only the DEFAULT subject; the dashboard's Who picker overrides it per job. Geometry comes from the identity, never from a target — this is the structural opposite of the face-zone lane.

reference_policy._rule: Real camera photos only (profile references.ground_truth). The job REFUSES if the subject has none — likeness is never conditioned on generated material.

template: {shot} of a person, {expression}, {wardrobe}, {setting}, {lighting}, {style}, sharp detailed facial features, natural skin texture, high detail
negative: text, letters, words, watermark, blurry, low quality, deformed face, distorted features, extra limbs, mutated hands, plastic skin, waxy, airbrushed, different person, mask, cgi doll

setting.label: Setting / scene (e.g. neon Tokyo street at night)

wardrobe.default: a black bomber jacket over a plain tee
wardrobe.label: Wardrobe

style.default: cinematic photography, 85mm, shallow depth of field
style.label: Style

lighting: soft key light with warm rim

rubric.identity: 1-5 — is this immediately recognizable as the SUBJECT's real reference photos, at normal viewing size (not only zoomed)?
rubric.face_integrity: 1-5 — eyes, mouth, jaw, ears, hair and skin coherent; no melting, no doubled features
rubric.realism: 1-5 — natural skin texture and lighting; not plastic or airbrushed
rubric.scene_quality: 1-5 — composition, lighting and setting read as intentional
